Subject: Refund still missing for returned coat

Hello,

I returned a wool coat from order 4471-ZK-20983 on 3 October using the prepaid label. The tracking shows it was delivered to your returns centre on 7 October and signed for by someone called Ruth Abernethy. Your policy says refunds go out within 14 days of receipt, but I still have not received the 89.90 pounds. The item was unworn with tags attached, and no restocking fee applies to coats.

Your agent, Dariusz Wróbel, told me on the phone last week that the refund was "approved but not released". When I asked Dariusz for a reference number, he said he couldn't give one. When I called back, a different agent said there was no record of the return at all.

Please reply to agnes.whitlow@example.com or call 07700 900418. My delivery address on the account is 12 Larch Mews, Harrowfield.

Agnes Whitlow
task: Help me turn this into a firmer complaint that asks for the refund by a clear deadline and sets out what each agent told me.

text:
Need help with a garage bill. Took my 2014 Corolla to a small independent garage (not the dealer) for a clutch judder. The owner, Kaveh Rostami, quoted 340 pounds for a clutch plate and said he would phone before doing anything else. He didn't phone. The invoice, INV-77812, came to 512 pounds, including 118 pounds for a flywheel I never approved and 54 pounds of 'diagnostics' that weren't on the quote.

Kaveh now says his apprentice, Lewis Achterberg, left a voicemail on 2 September, but I have no missed call or voicemail from that day. I've paid the 340 so I could get the car back, under protest, and the remaining 172 is outstanding. Kaveh's mobile is 07700 900662 if that matters. The garage is threatening a debt collector after 30 days.

What are my options?
task: What are my options for disputing the parts of this bill I didn't approve, and how should I word a message to the garage?

text:
Claim query – policy PX-PET-0093321

Policyholder: Hemi Tawhiri
Pet: Biscuit, 6-year-old border collie

Biscuit was seen at Riverside Vets on 19 September after swallowing part of a rubber toy. Dr Ngaio Pomare, the vet, removed it by endoscopy, so no surgery was needed. The total bill was 1,240 euros. Your letter of 2 October says you will pay only 610 euros because the procedure was 'preventable'. My policy covers foreign-body removal, and the excess is 150 euros, not the 250 euros your letter deducted.

Dr Pomare's clinical notes are attached and confirm the toy was a normal dog toy, not something unsafe. I can be reached at hemi.tawhiri@example.net. Bank details for any top-up payment: IBAN XX12 TEST 0000 4455 6677 01.
task: Help me write an appeal to my pet insurer explaining why the payout looks wrong, with the numbers laid out clearly.

text:
Hi Funmilayo,

I hope things are calmer at Hartwell Logistics since the restructure. I'm applying for an operations coordinator role at a freight company and they've asked for two references by Friday 13 November. Would you be willing to be one of them? You managed me for just over four years, from January 2022 until I left in March this year.

The recruiter, Saoirse Nic Giolla, will email you from saoirse.ng@recruit.example. Saoirse said the reference is a short form plus possibly a ten-minute call, and they won't contact you until you agree.

If it helps, I'd be grateful if you could mention the warehouse scheduling project, which cut late dispatches from about 9% to under 4%. Please don't feel obliged if you're too busy; I completely understand.

You can reach me on 07700 900275.

Thanks,
Tomás Ferreira-Ilunga

text:
Notes for my small-claims form (deadline 30 November):

- Decorator: Bram Okafor. Agreed price was 650 pounds for the hallway and stairs. I first wrote 600 in my email to him, but that was a typo; the signed quote says 650.
- I paid a 200-pound deposit on 1 August, not the full amount. Nothing else has been paid.
- Bram left after two days. The stairs were never painted, and the hallway needs a second coat.
- My husband, Jarek, spoke to Bram on 9 August. Bram told Jarek he would come back "within a fortnight". He didn't.
- My neighbour, Ama Mensah-Lindqvist, saw the unfinished work and might give a written statement, but only if it doesn't go to a hearing.
- Bram later offered to refund 100 pounds if I dropped the claim. I did not accept.
- I'm claiming the 200-pound deposit back plus 85 pounds for paint I bought myself.
task: Help me turn these notes into a clear statement of facts for the claim, in date order.

text:
I'm trying to decide between two phone deals and keep going round in circles.

Option 1: 24-month contract, 32 pounds a month, includes the phone (128 GB model), 100 GB data, EU roaming included. Leaving early means paying the remaining months.
Option 2: buy the same phone outright for 649 pounds and take a 12-month SIM-only plan at 12 pounds a month with 60 GB data and roaming at 2 pounds a day. After 12 months I'd expect a similar price on a new SIM-only deal.

I travel abroad maybe four times a year, usually for a week each time. I rarely go over 40 GB. I'd also like the freedom to switch networks next year if prices drop.

One more thing: the carrier's app keeps throwing "Error 503: Service Unavailable" when I try to check my usage, on app version 8.4.2. Is that something on my end or theirs?
task: Work out the total two-year cost of each option for my usage and tell me which makes more sense, plus what that app error usually means.
